topic: Advertising, Marketing Disclosures, and Consumer Notices
question: A Broker who is currently licensed and actively affiliated with XYZ Realty accepts a second, concurrent affiliation with ABC Realty without terminating the first. Under 4 CCR 725-1 Rule 6.10.A.1, what is true of this arrangement?
choice_a: It violates the rule, because a Broker may be licensed to conduct Real Estate Brokerage Services under only one Brokerage Firm at a time
choice_b: It is permitted as long as the Broker discloses both firms to consumers in writing
choice_c: It is permitted for up to 90 days while the Broker transitions between firms
choice_d: It is permitted only if the two firms are under common ownership
explanation: Rule 6.10.A.1 states that pursuant to section 12-10-203(9), C.R.S., no Broker will be licensed to conduct Real Estate Brokerage Services under more than one Brokerage Firm at the same time; a concurrent, undisclosed second affiliation violates the rule regardless of disclosure or duration.

topic: Advertising, Marketing Disclosures, and Consumer Notices
question: Under section 12-10-203(9), C.R.S., under what name may a person licensed as a real estate broker conduct or promote a real estate brokerage business?
choice_a: Under any Trade Name the Broker's firm has registered with a title company
choice_b: Only under the name under which the person is licensed
choice_c: Under any name the Broker chooses, provided it is not misleading
choice_d: Under the name of the Broker's sponsoring Employing Broker only
explanation: Section 12-10-203(9), C.R.S. provides that no person shall be licensed as a real estate broker under more than one name, and no person shall conduct or promote a real estate brokerage business except under the name under which the person is licensed.

topic: Advertising, Marketing Disclosures, and Consumer Notices
question: A Broker owns a residential property outright, and unlike the exempt scenario addressed by Rule 6.10.A.4, the Broker has listed that property for sale with the Broker's own Brokerage Firm. What follows under Rule 6.10?
choice_a: The Broker remains exempt from using the Brokerage Firm's name because the Broker personally owns the property
choice_b: The Broker may advertise under a Trade Name instead of the Brokerage Firm's name
choice_c: The exemption for advertising owner-occupied, unlisted property no longer applies, and the Broker must advertise the property clearly and conspicuously in the Brokerage Firm's name
choice_d: The Broker must obtain a second, separate license before advertising the listed property
explanation: The Rule 6.10.A.4 exemption applies only to real property owned by the Broker that is NOT listed for sale or lease with the Broker's Brokerage Firm. Once the Broker lists the property with the Firm, the general Rule 6.10.A.1 requirement to advertise clearly and conspicuously in the Brokerage Firm's name applies.

topic: Advertising, Marketing Disclosures, and Consumer Notices
question: A Brokerage Firm operates under a nationally franchised Trade Name owned by a third party. Which phrase, displayed clearly and conspicuously in the Firm's advertising, satisfies Rule 6.10.A.6.a?
choice_a: "[Trade Name] is a registered trademark used under license."
choice_b: "All rights reserved by [Trade Name] Corporate."
choice_c: "[Trade Name] assumes no liability for local franchisee conduct."
choice_d: "Each [Trade Name] brokerage business is independently owned and operated."
explanation: Rule 6.10.A.6.a requires a Brokerage Firm using a third-party Trade Name or Trademark to display, clearly and conspicuously, either "Each (insert general Trade Name) brokerage business is independently owned and operated" or "Each office independently owned and operated."

topic: Advertising, Marketing Disclosures, and Consumer Notices
question: A group of Brokers forming a Team within a Brokerage Firm wants a name that complies with Rule 6.10.B.1. Which of the following terms would NOT, by itself, cause the Team's name to violate the rule?
choice_a: "Group"
choice_b: "Realty"
choice_c: "LLC"
choice_d: "Company"
explanation: Rule 6.10.B.1 prohibits Teams from using terms such as "Realty," "Real estate," "Realtors," "Company," "Corporation," "Corp.," "Inc.," "LLC," "LP," or "LLP," or any other term implying a separate entity from the Brokerage Firm. "Group" does not appear on that prohibited list.

topic: Advertising, Marketing Disclosures, and Consumer Notices
question: A Listing Contract for a property advertised on a Broker's own website expires on the 1st of the month, and the Broker takes no action to remove it. On which date, at the latest, is the Broker in violation of Rule 6.10.D.1 if the listing is still displayed?
choice_a: The 8th of the month, since the Broker has a seven-day grace period
choice_b: The 4th of the month, since expired listings must be removed from Electronic Media the Broker owns or controls within three days of expiration
choice_c: The 31st of the month, since the Broker has a thirty-day grace period
choice_d: There is no violation, since Rule 6.10.D.1 only applies to sold listings, not expired ones
explanation: Rule 6.10.D.1 requires that expired listings be removed from a Broker's Electronic Media within three days of a Listing Contract expiring, so a listing still displayed more than three days after expiration is a violation.

topic: Advertising, Marketing Disclosures, and Consumer Notices
question: Rule 6.10.D.1's three-day removal requirement for expired listings applies to which Electronic Media?
choice_a: Every website anywhere on the internet that happens to display the listing
choice_b: Only the Multiple Listing Service, and no other Electronic Media
choice_c: Electronic Media that the Broker owns or controls, such as the Broker's own website
choice_d: Only printed advertising, not Electronic Media
explanation: Rule 6.10.D.1 addresses Electronic Media owned or controlled by the Broker; the Broker is responsible for removing expired listings from media within that Broker's own ownership or control, not from every third-party site that may have republished the listing.

topic: Advertising, Marketing Disclosures, and Consumer Notices
question: Rule 6.10.D.4's "first click of the mouse" disclosure standard applies specifically to which situation?
choice_a: Any Electronic Media, regardless of available space
choice_b: Print advertising only
choice_c: Advertising for commercial, but not residential, property
choice_d: Electronic Media where space is so limited that it is not reasonable to disclose the Broker's, Team's, and Brokerage Firm's names directly on the page
explanation: Rule 6.10.D.4 provides that when it is not reasonable to disclose the Broker's or Team's name and the Brokerage Firm's name directly in Electronic Media because space is limited, the Broker must disclose that information clearly and conspicuously within the first click of the mouse.

topic: Advertising, Marketing Disclosures, and Consumer Notices
question: A Brokerage Firm publishes an advertisement recapping average sale prices over the past year for a particular county. Under Rule 6.10.E, what must this advertisement include?
choice_a: The source of the data
choice_b: A notarized statement from the county assessor
choice_c: The Brokerage Firm's errors and omissions insurance policy number
choice_d: A list of every property included in the data
explanation: Rule 6.10.E requires that general sales data advertising recapping sales activity over a period of time in a subdivision or geographical area cite the source of the data, in addition to including a disclaimer if accurate.

topic: Advertising, Marketing Disclosures, and Consumer Notices
question: A Broker advertises a home's square footage using figures pulled from the county assessor's records. Under Rule 6.11, how must the Broker disclose this source to Consumers?
choice_a: Only in the Multiple Listing Service confidential remarks
choice_b: On the Commission-Approved Form
choice_c: The Broker need not disclose the source if it came from a government record
choice_d: By email to the buyer's lender only
explanation: Rule 6.11 requires the Broker to disclose the source of the square footage of the floor space of the living area to Consumers on the Commission-Approved Form, regardless of where the underlying figure originated.

topic: Advertising, Marketing Disclosures, and Consumer Notices
question: A Broker prepares a Broker's Price Opinion for a client settling an estate, not for an anticipated sale or purchase. Under Rule 6.12, what must appear on that BPO?
choice_a: A notice that the BPO is legally equivalent to a certified appraisal
choice_b: A notice waiving the Broker's liability for any errors in the opinion
choice_c: A notice stating the evaluation was prepared by a licensed real estate broker, is not an appraisal, and cannot be used for the purposes of obtaining financing
choice_d: No notice is required because the BPO was not prepared for a sale
explanation: Rule 6.12 requires the specified notice on a CMA or BPO prepared for a reason other than the anticipated sale or purchase of the property, including estate settlement purposes.

topic: Advertising, Marketing Disclosures, and Consumer Notices
question: Under section 12-10-602(9)(b)(II), C.R.S., a Broker's opinion of value is excluded from the definition of an appraisal, and the Broker need not be licensed as an appraiser, only if the opinion meets what conditions?
choice_a: It is prepared free of charge and reviewed by a supervising broker
choice_b: It is limited to properties valued under $500,000
choice_c: It is prepared only for properties the Broker personally owns
choice_d: It is not represented as an appraisal, and it is not used for purposes of obtaining financing
explanation: Section 12-10-602(9)(b)(II), C.R.S. excludes from the definition of "appraiser" a person licensed as a broker who provides an opinion of value that is not represented as an appraisal and is not used for purposes of obtaining financing.

topic: Advertising, Marketing Disclosures, and Consumer Notices
question: A lender asks a Broker to prepare a Comparative Market Analysis to help support a loan application, and the Broker complies. What is the effect under section 12-10-602(9)(b)(II), C.R.S.?
choice_a: The Broker's opinion of value no longer qualifies for the broker exclusion, because it was used for the purposes of obtaining financing
choice_b: There is no effect, because Brokers are always permitted to supply valuations for financing purposes
choice_c: The CMA automatically becomes a certified appraisal for legal purposes
choice_d: The lender, not the Broker, bears sole responsibility for any resulting violation
explanation: Because section 12-10-602(9)(b)(II), C.R.S. excludes a broker's opinion of value from appraiser licensure only when it is not used for obtaining financing, using a CMA or BPO for that purpose defeats the exclusion.

topic: Advertising, Marketing Disclosures, and Consumer Notices
question: A Broker wants to buy, rather than sell, real property on the Broker's own account. Under Rule 6.17.B, what must the Broker do?
choice_a: Nothing, because Rule 6.17.B only applies when a Broker is selling property
choice_b: Disclose that they are a licensed Broker in the contracting instrument or in a separate concurrent writing
choice_c: Obtain prior written approval from the Real Estate Commission
choice_d: Wait 30 days after obtaining the license before purchasing property
explanation: Rule 6.17.B requires a Broker who sells, buys, or leases real property on the Broker's own account to disclose that they are a licensed Broker in the contracting instrument or in a separate concurrent writing; the disclosure requirement applies to buying just as it does to selling.

topic: Advertising, Marketing Disclosures, and Consumer Notices
question: An Employing Broker plans to refer a Consumer to a title company that is part of an Affiliated Business Arrangement. Under Rule 6.18.A, by when must the existence of that arrangement be disclosed to the Consumer?
choice_a: Within ten business days after the referral is made
choice_b: No later than the closing date
choice_c: At or prior to the time the referral is made
choice_d: Only if the Consumer specifically asks about the relationship
explanation: Rule 6.18.A requires disclosure of the existence of an Affiliated Business Arrangement to the Consumer being referred at or prior to the time the referral is made, and the disclosure must comply with RESPA.

topic: Advertising, Marketing Disclosures, and Consumer Notices
question: Section 12-10-218(1), C.R.S. defines "associate," for purposes of identifying an Affiliated Business Arrangement, to include which of the following?
choice_a: Only individuals who are married to the referring licensee
choice_b: Only corporations in which the licensee owns 51% or more
choice_c: Only other licensees within the same Brokerage Firm
choice_d: Spouses, parents, children, related business entities, employers, officers, directors, partners, franchisers, and franchisees who could benefit financially from a referral
explanation: Section 12-10-218(1), C.R.S. defines "associate" broadly to include spouses, parents, children, related business entities, employers, officers, directors, partners, franchisers, franchisees, or anyone with an understanding enabling them to benefit financially from referrals.

topic: Advertising, Marketing Disclosures, and Consumer Notices
question: Under section 12-10-218(2), C.R.S., may a licensee require a Consumer to use an affiliated settlement service provider as a condition of receiving brokerage services?
choice_a: No, licensees cannot require use of affiliated businesses or specific providers as a condition of providing services
choice_b: Yes, provided the requirement is disclosed in writing
choice_c: Yes, but only for Consumers who are financing the purchase
choice_d: Yes, provided the Consumer receives a discount for using the affiliate
explanation: Section 12-10-218(2), C.R.S. prohibits licensees from requiring Consumers to use an affiliated business or a specific settlement service provider as a condition of receiving services.

topic: Advertising, Marketing Disclosures, and Consumer Notices
question: Section 12-10-218(2), C.R.S. prohibits kickbacks in an Affiliated Business Arrangement, but which of the following payments remains permissible?
choice_a: A flat referral fee paid to the Broker for each Consumer sent to the affiliate, regardless of services performed
choice_b: A payment to a title agent, attorney, or lender for services actually performed
choice_c: A percentage of the affiliate's net profit paid to the Broker solely for the referral
choice_d: A gift card given to the Broker in exchange for steering Consumers to the affiliate
explanation: Under section 12-10-218(2), C.R.S., an Affiliated Business Arrangement is permitted, and kickbacks are prohibited, but legitimate payments to attorneys, title agents, and lenders for actual services rendered remain permissible.

topic: Advertising, Marketing Disclosures, and Consumer Notices
question: Under section 12-10-218, C.R.S., in addition to disclosing an Affiliated Business Arrangement when it is entered into or changed, what recurring obligation does an Employing Broker have?
choice_a: The Employing Broker must re-disclose the arrangement before every single transaction
choice_b: The Employing Broker has no recurring disclosure obligation once the initial disclosure is made
choice_c: The Employing Broker must make an annual disclosure of the arrangement, including physical locations
choice_d: The Employing Broker must disclose the arrangement only if the Division of Real Estate requests it
explanation: Section 12-10-218(3)-(4), C.R.S. requires licensees to disclose affiliated arrangements upon entry into or change of the arrangement, and requires Employing Brokers to make an annual disclosure, including physical locations.

topic: Advertising, Marketing Disclosures, and Consumer Notices
question: A Broker sees a competing firm's listing and, without contacting the owner or the listing Broker, posts the property's price and availability on the Broker's own social media to generate leads. What does Rule 6.10.F say about this?
choice_a: This is permitted, because any publicly listed property may be advertised by any licensed Broker
choice_b: This is permitted as long as the Broker's ad links back to the original listing
choice_c: This is permitted only in markets with a Multiple Listing Service cooperation agreement
choice_d: Brokers may not advertise the availability or price of a property without authority from the owner or the owner's Broker, and must disclose the owner's Brokerage Firm
explanation: Rule 6.10.F states that Brokers may not advertise the availability or price of a property, whether for sale or lease, without authority from the owner or the owner's Broker and disclosure of the owner's Brokerage Firm.

topic: Advertising, Marketing Disclosures, and Consumer Notices
question: Under section 12-10-217(1)(a), C.R.S., a Broker who knowingly makes use of false or misleading advertising may face which of the following, after a hearing before the Commission?
choice_a: An administrative fine of up to $2,500 per offense, censure, probation, suspension, or revocation of license
choice_b: A mandatory criminal misdemeanor charge only
choice_c: Automatic, permanent revocation with no right to a hearing
choice_d: A civil penalty payable directly to the harmed Consumer only, with no license action
explanation: Section 12-10-217(1)(a), C.R.S. makes knowingly making any misrepresentation or knowingly making use of false or misleading advertising grounds for discipline; the Commission may, after a hearing, impose an administrative fine of up to $2,500 per offense along with censure, probation, suspension, or revocation.

topic: Advertising, Marketing Disclosures, and Consumer Notices
question: A Broker publishes an advertisement containing an inaccurate square footage figure because a third-party data vendor supplied incorrect information, and the Broker has no reason to doubt its accuracy. Does this alone establish a violation of section 12-10-217(1)(a), C.R.S.?
choice_a: Yes, the statute imposes strict liability regardless of the Broker's knowledge
choice_b: Not necessarily, because that subsection targets a Broker who knowingly makes a misrepresentation or knowingly uses false or misleading advertising
choice_c: Yes, but only if the inaccurate figure increased the sale price
choice_d: No, because section 12-10-217(1)(a) applies only to advertising prepared entirely in-house
explanation: Section 12-10-217(1)(a), C.R.S. is worded to require that the Broker "knowingly" make a misrepresentation or "knowingly" use false or misleading advertising; an innocent reliance on inaccurate third-party data, without more, does not by itself establish that knowing element.

topic: Advertising, Marketing Disclosures, and Consumer Notices
question: What is the primary purpose of the "independently owned and operated" disclosure required by Rule 6.10.A.6.a when a Brokerage Firm advertises under a third-party Trade Name?
choice_a: To satisfy federal trademark registration requirements
choice_b: To allow the Brokerage Firm to charge a higher commission
choice_c: To prevent Consumers from being misled into believing the local Brokerage Firm is the same legal entity as the national franchise or Trade Name owner
choice_d: To exempt the Brokerage Firm from the Commission's advertising rules entirely
explanation: The Rule 6.10.A.6.a disclosure exists to prevent Consumer confusion between a locally owned Brokerage Firm operating under a licensed Trade Name and the separate entity that owns that Trade Name.

topic: Advertising, Marketing Disclosures, and Consumer Notices
question: A Broker advertises a property's square footage but simply tells the Consumer "the number came from somewhere reliable," without identifying a specific source or using the Commission-Approved Form. Does this satisfy Rule 6.11?
choice_a: Yes, any verbal assurance of reliability satisfies the rule
choice_b: Yes, because Rule 6.11 only applies to commercial property
choice_c: Yes, provided the square footage figure turns out to be accurate
choice_d: No, Rule 6.11 requires the source of the square footage to be disclosed to Consumers on the Commission-Approved Form, not through a vague verbal assurance
explanation: Rule 6.11 specifically requires disclosure of the source of the square footage on the Commission-Approved Form; a vague verbal assurance without an identified source and without using the required form does not satisfy the rule.

topic: Advertising, Marketing Disclosures, and Consumer Notices
question: Why does Rule 6.10.B.1 prohibit a Team from using terms like "Realty," "Company," "Inc.," or "LLC" in its name?
choice_a: To prevent Consumers from being misled into thinking the Team is a separate licensed brokerage entity, rather than a group operating within the Brokerage Firm
choice_b: To prevent Teams from competing with the Brokerage Firm for the same listings
choice_c: To reserve those terms exclusively for out-of-state brokerages
choice_d: To ensure every Team eventually becomes its own licensed Brokerage Firm
explanation: Rule 6.10.B.1's prohibition on entity-implying terms in Team names is intended to prevent Consumers from mistakenly believing the Team is itself a separately licensed Brokerage Firm, rather than a group of Brokers operating under the actual Brokerage Firm.

topic: Advertising, Marketing Disclosures, and Consumer Notices
question: Rule 6.18.A requires that the disclosure of an Affiliated Business Arrangement comply with which federal law's format and content requirements?
choice_a: The Truth in Lending Act (TILA)
choice_b: The Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act (RESPA)
choice_c: The Fair Housing Act
choice_d: The Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform Act
explanation: Rule 6.18.A requires that the Affiliated Business Arrangement disclosure comply with RESPA, consistent with 12-10-218(2)(b), C.R.S., which directs the Commission's rules to adopt federal HUD/RESPA guidelines.

topic: Advertising, Marketing Disclosures, and Consumer Notices
question: Section 12-10-218(1), C.R.S. defines "settlement service," for purposes of the Affiliated Business Arrangement statute, broadly enough to include which of the following?
choice_a: Only mortgage loan origination services
choice_b: Only services provided directly by the Colorado Real Estate Commission
choice_c: Title searches and examinations, title insurance, attorney services, appraisals, home inspections, real estate brokerage, and loan origination and closing services
choice_d: Only title insurance and nothing else
explanation: Section 12-10-218(1), C.R.S. defines "settlement service" broadly to encompass title searches, examinations, and insurance; attorney services; document preparation; surveys; credit reports; appraisals; home inspections; real estate brokerage; pest inspections; and loan origination, processing, underwriting, funding, escrow, and closing services.

topic: Advertising, Marketing Disclosures, and Consumer Notices
question: Under section 12-10-217(2), C.R.S., a rental location agent must provide a prospective tenant with a contract that includes what, displayed in prominent letters?
choice_a: The rental location agent's personal cell phone number
choice_b: A list of every property the agent currently represents
choice_c: The landlord's Social Security number for verification
choice_d: The address and telephone number of the Commission
explanation: Section 12-10-217(2), C.R.S. requires rental location agents to provide prospective tenants a contract that includes the address and telephone number of the Commission in prominent letters, giving Consumers a clear path to file a complaint.

topic: Advertising, Marketing Disclosures, and Consumer Notices
question: Which exact statement does Rule 6.12 require to appear on a Comparative Market Analysis or Broker's Price Opinion prepared for a reason other than anticipated sale or purchase?
choice_a: "This evaluation was prepared by a licensed real estate broker and is not an appraisal. This evaluation cannot be used for the purposes of obtaining financing."
choice_b: "This evaluation is an unofficial estimate only and creates no duties whatsoever."
choice_c: "This evaluation was prepared at the request of, and paid for by, the Consumer."
choice_d: "This evaluation supersedes any prior appraisal of the property."
explanation: Rule 6.12 requires this precise notice, which both identifies the preparer as a licensed broker and warns that the evaluation is not an appraisal and cannot be used to obtain financing, consistent with the appraiser-licensure exclusion in 12-10-602(9)(b)(II), C.R.S.

topic: Advertising, Marketing Disclosures, and Consumer Notices
question: A Broker who is licensed under Brokerage Firm A begins conducting brokerage transactions under Brokerage Firm B's name without ending the affiliation with Firm A. Besides violating Rule 6.10.A.1, what statutory requirement under section 12-10-203(9), C.R.S. is also implicated?
choice_a: The requirement that a Broker complete 24 hours of continuing education before switching firms
choice_b: The requirement that a person conduct or promote a real estate brokerage business only under the name under which the person is licensed
choice_c: The requirement that a Broker maintain errors and omissions insurance
choice_d: The requirement that a Broker post a surety bond with the Commission
explanation: Section 12-10-203(9), C.R.S. requires that a person conduct or promote a real estate brokerage business only under the name under which the person is licensed, and Rule 6.10.A.1 implements that requirement by limiting a Broker to one Brokerage Firm at a time.
